{NICKNAME}: That's the scientific name, of course.
Paimon: Oh? What would the common name be then?
{NICKNAME}: "Noisy Two-Legged Critter"
Paimon: Hey! Why keep only the negative traits?
voices.title: About Sumpter Beasts

voices.text:
Paimon: There are six Darshans in Sumeru.
Paimon: It would be cool if Paimon had her own Darshan too!
Paimon: It'll be called... Paimonology!
{NICKNAME}: And... what wisdom would Paimonology stand for?
Paimon: Uh... practical wisdom for everyday life!
{NICKNAME}: So Paimonology scholars would specialize in the art of cooking slimes in a hundred different ways, and never letting a single Mora escape their grasp, and giving people ugly nicknames... et cetera, et cetera?
Paimon: Whoa, you read Paimon's mind! Also, don't forget "How to Become the Best Travel Guide in Teyvat"!
Paimon: This is a fantastic idea! Come on, let's go submit a Darshan application to the Akademiya! From this day on, {NICKNAME}'ll be the Grand Sage of Paimonology!
{NICKNAME}: I'd like to decline the honor, please...
voices.title: About the Seventh Darshan

voices.text:
Paimon: Did you know that there are all kinds of strange Shroom-Kin in Sumeru?
{NICKNAME}: Yup. Here's a fun one — legend has it that there were some forest boars who couldn't live without mushrooms, and the two species gradually formed a symbiotic relationship with each other. Now they're known as "Shroomboars."
Paimon: Whoa, that's a lot like us! Paimon can't live without {NICKNAME} either.
{NICKNAME}: If you can't live without me, that means... I'm the shroom, and Paimon's the...
Paimon: Boar!
Paimon: Hey, wait a second...
voices.title: About Shroomboars

voices.text:
Paimon: The residents of the Grand Bazaar are all so talented!
Paimon: They sell their own woven goods, beautiful vases and jars, and delicious-smelling spices that make Paimon's tummy start rumbling...
Paimon: And they all sing and dance really well! Paimon wishes she could do that.
{NICKNAME}: Well, if you're serious about it, there's no reason you couldn't learn.
Paimon: What? Really?
{NICKNAME}: Well for starters, you have a natural advantage when it comes to dancing.
{NICKNAME}: You won't trip over yourself, or accidentally step on someone's foot...
Paimon: Oh yeah! Paimon always forgets how useful flying can be!
Paimon: Alright then! Let's go bust a move at the Grand Bazaar and watch everyone shower Paimon with admiration!
{NICKNAME}: Aha, so that's what this is all about.
voices.title: About the Grand Bazaar

voices.text:
Paimon: People in Sumeru seem to take divination and fortune-telling pretty seriously.
Paimon: For starters, there's astrology, although only the scholars get to practice that. But ordinary citizens have their ways, too. They can do divinations with just a cup of coffee!
{NICKNAME}: It's the nation of wisdom after all. It seems like people have an insatiable curiosity to learn about everything, including their own future.
Paimon: Paimon heard that they can tell your fate just by looking at the bottom of a finished cup of coffee...
Paimon: Sounds way easier than climbing to the top of a tower and staring at the stars all night!
{NICKNAME}: Oh, so you're interested in learning your fate now?
Paimon: Yeah... although, Paimon's really more interested in finding out what the coffee tastes like.
voices.title: About Divination

voices.text:
Paimon: Khedive and Anisa kept talking about "Purbiruni" this and "Pursina" that...
Paimon: Why do all these words have "pur" at the front?
{NICKNAME}: "Pur" means "descendant," and also "student"... So in this case, they're referring to themselves as the children and students of the great sages of old.
Paimon: Huh, so that's what it means... From the way they were throwing these words around, Paimon was sure it'd be something to be proud of.
{NICKNAME}: Wait... But isn't it?
Paimon: Well, Paimon for one would much rather be known as the founding father than have a name that basically says "So-and-so's my daddy." Pretty embarrassing, don't you think?
{NICKNAME}: Um... Yeah, I have to admit, I've never thought about it like that...
voices.title: About Purbiruni and Pursina

voices.text:
Paimon: It's not only Sumeru locals at the Akademiya, huh. There are students from other nations too.
Paimon: Imagine leaving your hometown behind and traveling to a faraway and unfamiliar land in the pursuit of learning... How inspiring!
{NICKNAME}: We travel to unfamiliar lands pretty often, too.
Paimon: Huh, you're right! That means we're also super inspiring!
{NICKNAME}: Not in the pursuit of learning, though.
Paimon: Oh... So we're not as inspiring as the students after all...
Paimon: Buuut we do know the best places to eat in Sumeru, and who you can rely on to help you out! That counts as knowledge, right?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, and to many people, it could be extremely valuable knowledge.
Paimon: Great, so we're just as inspiring as them after all!
voices.title: About Studying Abroad

voices.text:
Paimon: The whole of Sumeru City is built on top of a giant tree. How amazing is that!
Paimon: We've seen lots of incredible trees on our journey, haven't we? There's our old stomping ground at Windrise, the Frostbearing Tree on Dragonspine, and the Sacred Sakura in Inazuma!
Paimon: Sumeru's tree doesn't seem to have a fancy name though. People just call it "the Divine Tree"...
{NICKNAME}: Sometimes, the most important things have the simplest names.
Paimon: Really? Hmm, maybe you have a point. Long names would be kinda inconvenient if you had to say them every day.
Paimon: Anyway, people in the city only have to say "down below" and everyone knows they mean the bottom of the tree.
Paimon: What's that saying again? "Names aren't things themselves, they're just words for things."
{NICKNAME}: So is Paimon just a word for a thing, too?
Paimon: Yeah. Well, uh, kinda. But... wait, no! No, Paimon is just Paimon!
voices.title: About the Divine Tree

voices.text:
Paimon: So, with Sumeru having so many scholars in different Darshans, do you think they end up arguing a lot?
Paimon: You know, just like the rivalry between Li cuisine and Yue cuisine in Liyue.
{NICKNAME}: I'm sure they do. Conflict between different schools of thought is the most normal thing ever. As the Liyue martial arts novels say: "Wherever there are people, there will be conflict."
Paimon: Wow, what a line. That's heavy... But the scholars in Sumeru probably don't duel like Liyue martial artists, right?
{NICKNAME}: Maybe they settle things with a game of Genius Invokation TCG.
Paimon: Ohh, good point! A duel of wits!
Paimon: Paimon can just imagine it: When one scholar can't convince another in an argument, he takes out his deck of cards, calmly sits down opposite his opponent, thinks for a moment, and then secures his victory!
{NICKNAME}: That does sound like something that would happen in Sumeru.
Paimon: The game ends, and the winner says "good game" as a sign of respect to his opponent. After that, both sides are back on good terms.
{NICKNAME}: Umm, not necessarily...
Paimon: Huh? Why?
voices.title: About Inter-Darshan Relations

voices.text:
Paimon: Whew, Port Ormos definitely has a different vibe to Sumeru City...
Paimon: It's a bustling area, and there's so many outlanders. Plus, no one needs to spend all their time buried in their studies, which is nice.
{NICKNAME}: Yes, but that's why they end up being disciplined by the port authorities. So you see, Paimon? If you don't study hard, you'll end up just like them!
Paimon: Oh...
Paimon: Wait! What was that tone of voice for!?
voices.title: About Port Ormos

voices.text:
Paimon: Port Ormos is built on the ruins of the fortress of The Alliance of the... the... the alliance of something, anyway.
Paimon: Ugh, the name's too long, Paimon can't remember it! Anyway, that's what all the bookish people in Sumeru say.
{NICKNAME}: Oh, you mean "The Alliance of the Twenty-Nine Ocean Deys"?
{NICKNAME}: Apparently, the alliance was formed by a bunch of arrogant pirate leaders, none of whom wanted to work for any of the others. They fought and looted each other constantly, causing endless chaos in coastal Sumeru...
{NICKNAME}: Finally, one day, they decided to enter into an alliance with one another and divide power equally between themselves. The members of the alliance were called "Deys"...
Paimon: Oh... And so after that... there was no more fighting and no more stealing, so everyone could get along happily and make a boatload of Mora together! Right?
{NICKNAME}: ...
Paimon: Right...?
{NICKNAME}: Well... presumably that's what they were hoping...
Paimon: Huh...?
{NICKNAME}: Before long, they were forming factions again, and the infighting between them escalated into the biggest internal battle they'd seen yet. Their fortress at Port Ormos was completely destroyed, and all the Deys were done for!
Paimon: Whaaat?
{NICKNAME}: Following that, an unprecedented period of peace finally came to Port Ormos, and the area began to develop into what we see today...
Paimon: Huh... So the Alliance was just a bunch of dumb bad guys...
voices.title: About the Alliance of the Twenty-Nine Ocean Deys

voices.text:
Paimon: Cyno's super into that card game "Genius Invokation TCG," isn't he?
Paimon: Doesn't it seem kinda weird for the General Mahamatra to be into playing cards...?
{NICKNAME}: Well... not when you consider his hairstyle.
Paimon: Huh? What has his hairstyle got to do with it?
{NICKNAME}: You know, when you're playing a card game, the fancier your hairstyle, the more distracting it is for your opponent.
{NICKNAME}: "What's going on with this guy? How did he manage to shape his hair like that?"
{NICKNAME}: When your opponent's mind is consumed with thoughts like this, you'll quickly gain the upper hand.
Paimon: Hmm, really? Then we'd better think twice before playing against him...
{NICKNAME}: I don't know... I think I might just have an advantage over him.
Paimon: But you don't have a fancy hairstyle at all. And your clothes look pretty normal, too...
{NICKNAME}: But I do have Paimon.
{NICKNAME}: "What's up with her? And what's that pesky flying companion of hers up to?"
{NICKNAME}: As long as Paimon is floating by my side, Cyno's mind will be consumed with thoughts like this.
{NICKNAME}: I, on the other hand, would be completely unfazed by his hairstyle. So I'd be able to focus, and victory would be mine.
Paimon: Forget it! If you wanna play cards, go get a funny haircut!
voices.title: About Cyno and Genius Invokation TCG...

voices.text:
Paimon: ♪ Curry, curry, in the air~ Hungry children it's time to come home~ ♪
{NICKNAME}: ♪ Curry, curry, in the air~ ♪
Paimon: Wow! Good job, so you remember the tune as well!
{NICKNAME}: Good job to you too, Paimon. You sing really well.
Paimon: Heehee, that's because Paimon's got a great plan!
Paimon: Have you heard this story? Once upon a time, there was a hilihound who was given meat to eat whenever the samachurls started dancing. Eventually, the hilihound started drooling whenever it heard the sound of dancing.
Paimon: Whenever we hear the curry song, we get curry to eat. So, all Paimon has to do is learn the song by heart, and then in the future, whenever Paimon is craving a big bowl of tasty curry, all she has to do is sing it!
Paimon: Hey, aren't you gonna say something?
Paimon: ♪ Curry, curry, in the air~ Hungry children it's time to come home~ ♪
voices.title: About Sumeru Nursery Rhymes...

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: Paimon, do you ever find that the word "Aranara" trips you up?
Paimon: Hmm? Why, does it trip you up? Maybe that's because you don't really say anything most of the time.
Paimon: Unlike Paimon! Paimon has to talk all the time, so she never gets stuck on words.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, well, try reading this then.
Paimon: What is it? Let's see here...
Paimon: Arana the Aranara exercises Ararakalari in the nearby area.
Paimon: Narana the Nara picks Padisarahs in a parallel area further afield.
Paimon: Narana the Padisarah-picking Nara had arranged to invite Arana the Aranara to the bar to befriend Lambad, but alas, Arana the Ararakalari-exercising Aranara professed a preference to Padisarah-picking Nara, Narana, for venturing to Vanarana to view the panorama.
Paimon: On account of Arana the Aranara's antipathy to bar drama, Narana the Nara relented and, upon accompanying the latter on a Vanarana-panorama adventure, encountered another Aranara, named "Arama."
Paimon: This must be one of those really weird dreams, right...
Paimon: Ugh, but this headache feels pretty real...
voices.title: About Aranara Tongue Twisters...

voices.text: Ha!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XIII

voices.text: Go!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XIV

voices.text: Water jet!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XV

voices.text: Ha!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XIII

voices.text: Wipeout!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XIV

voices.text: Bombs away!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XV

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon just thought of a great way to deal with Fontaine's prophesied crisis!
{NICKNAME}: Okay, let's hear it.
Paimon: You know those great big clockwork meka they use for digging tunnels? Well, why not send them deep underwater and get them to dig a load of drainage holes? Then no one'll have to worry about the water level rising anymore.
{NICKNAME}: Sounds logical enough, but where do you think the water will go?
Paimon: Ah, what does that matter! Think of it like... a coin pouch. When there's a hole in it, what's the use in racking your brains trying to figure out where all the Mora went? 'Cause the fact is, a coin pouch with a hole wouldn't be able to hold it all anyway.
{NICKNAME}: Well, I'd certainly like to know where all my Mora goes. But from what you're saying, it doesn't sound like you keep track...
Paimon: Hey, what's that supposed to mean? Paimon doesn't know where your... uh, P—Paimon doesn't know where your... Mora goes... hehe, heh...
voices.title: About the Prophesied Crisis...

voices.text:
Paimon: Lyney's magic shows are amazing! Paimon never would've guessed how he did it before he revealed his secret.
{NICKNAME}: Hold on... I just thought of a magic trick!
Paimon: Huh? You know how to do magic too?
{NICKNAME}: Yep. I can make a big magician's hat float in the air, and even make it move at my command.
Paimon: Whoa! Really? How do you do that?
{NICKNAME}: Hehe, simple! I put Paimon inside the hat.
Paimon: What? Why would Paimon be... Ohhh, so Paimon's the one making it float!
Paimon: Hehe, in that case, Paimon has an idea for an even better magic trick!
{NICKNAME}: Huh? What is it?
Paimon: Behold, the bottomless hat! No matter how many plates of delicious food you throw into it, it'll never get full!
{NICKNAME}: Uh... Wait, so where would the plates go?
Paimon: Oh, good point! Umm... Oh, the hat spits the empty plates back out! Tada! Whaddya think?
voices.title: About Magic...

voices.text:
Paimon: Fontaine's aquabuses are pretty cool. But imagine if they could run without tracks. Then you could go anywhere you want pretty much without having to move a muscle! Traveling would be way less tiring.
{NICKNAME}: But you already fly everywhere. Does that even get tiring?
Paimon: Fly... Fly? Wait, that's it! If we could find a way to make the boats float in the air, then they wouldn't need rails anymore. Hehe, and we could call them "airboats"!
Paimon: C'mon, let's go apply for one of those, uh... oh yeah — "patents"! We can't let Paimon's genius go to waste. Quick, before someone else beats us to it!
{NICKNAME}: Patents don't work like that... You can't just have a name for your invention. You also need to provide details of the original technical solution that makes your airboats float.
Paimon: Technical, huh? Hmm... Okay, got it! We just need to attach a giant propeller on top of the boats!
{NICKNAME}: Okay... But how would you prevent the boat from spinning along with the propeller? And how would you control the direction of movement?
Paimon: Um... Uh... Ugh. Paimon never realized flying was so complicated! It's always been second nature to Paimon...
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... Well, there might be an easier solution if we ditch the direction and speed control requirements?
Paimon: Huh? Really!?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah. It involves starting at a high altitude and flying downwards at a rapidly-increasing velocity.
Paimon: Hey! That isn't flying, that's free-falling!
voices.title: About Patented Flying Technology...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Steambird's Great Detective Hurlock series is gonna be published by Yae Publishing House, right?
{NICKNAME}: Seems like it.
Paimon: But The Steambird clearly doesn't need help with printing and distribution. Why don't they just publish it themselves?
{NICKNAME}: Hehehe, you still have a lot to learn about the dark side of the publishing industry...
Paimon: Ugh, okay, you know-it-all! Go on then, give Paimon one good reason why The Steambird can't publish its own novels, when it already publishes a newspaper that's read all over Teyvat.
{NICKNAME}: Because the key to a successful light novel is...
Paimon: Uh-huh?
{NICKNAME}: The illustrations!
Paimon: What!? No way. Try telling that to all the writers and editors in Teyvat! They're the ones working their butts off coming up with ideas!
{NICKNAME}: Maybe so, but the Yae Publishing House has all the best illustrators on their payroll, and poaching them can't be easy. Artists like Calx must be virtually impossible to contact without going through them.
Paimon: Ohhh... Yeah, that's a fair point.
{NICKNAME}: Mm-hmm. But there's another reason, too...
Paimon: Hm?
{NICKNAME}: Only works published by the Yae Publishing House make it into Genius Invokation TCG crossovers!
Paimon: Huh, Paimon never knew!
{NICKNAME}: That's the deepest, darkest secret of the publishing industry: It's not about stories anymore, it's about products and how to commercialize them.
Paimon: Hmph! That's just... sickening!
voices.title: About the Dark Side of Publishing...

voices.text:
Paimon: So apparently, some detectives in Fontaine manage to solve cases without ever setting foot outside their homes. They call them "armchair detectives"...
Paimon: That's what they call "working from home," right? Sounds pretty cushy.
Paimon: Still, how do they figure out the truth if they never even go to the crime scene? ...Oh, Paimon knows! They must be using divination.
{NICKNAME}: You're thinking of fortune-tellers, Paimon. Not detectives.
Paimon: Oh... yeah...
{NICKNAME}: In any case, surely the evidence isn't just dropping itself off at the detective's doorstep.
Paimon: You mean... Oh, the detective must have people collecting information for them...
{NICKNAME}: Perhaps, or... Maybe they post commissions at the Adventurers' Guild?
Paimon: Huh? But... that would mean the detective gets all the credit for our hard work! Bet they make a tidy sum of Mora off of it, too! Hmph, Paimon won't stand for that. Let's go have a little talk with Detective Armchair right now!
voices.title: About Armchair Detectives...

voices.text:
Paimon: At the Fontaine Research Institute, they research clockwork and different energy sources, right? So how come there are rumors about a mystery treasure?
Paimon: It'd make more sense if the treasure was owned by a bandit or a pirate.
Paimon: But Paimon's not sure that the researchers' and technicians' definition of "treasure" is really mysterious enough to get excited about...
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... What about "researcher by day, bandit by night"? Does that sound mysterious enough?
Paimon: Umm... Well for starters, it sounds exhausting. Imagine finishing your day job, then working a whole other job all night... When would they get time to rest?
{NICKNAME}: Maybe they wouldn't need to rest... If they were actually a clockwork meka in disguise!
Paimon: Ooh! A mystery treasure left by a clockwork meka who's a researcher by day and a bandit by night... Now that sounds more like it!
voices.title: About the Mysterious Treasure of the Fontaine Research Institute...

voices.text:
Paimon: Detective stories like "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are really popular in Fontaine.
{NICKNAME}: They're also pretty complex. Can you even follow the plot?
Paimon: Don't you underestimate Paimon! If Paimon read any of those novels, she'd definitely solve the mystery before she's even halfway through.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, well if you do, then keep it to yourself. You don't want to spoil the story for anyone else.
Paimon: Paimon would never do that!
{NICKNAME}: Although you also have to watch out for people who use "no spoilers" as an excuse to shut down discussions, when the truth is, they're just annoyed that a story they can't stand is getting so much attention.
Paimon: Huh. Well, Paimon doesn't read much, so she wouldn't know anything about that kinda thing.
{NICKNAME}: You see it a lot when two fans of Onibudou get talking. Someone'll butt in and say something like, "Stop, don't spoil it for me! I'm only up to chapter two of volume one!"
Paimon: Chapter two? Hah, yeah, clearly they have no intention of reading any further.
{NICKNAME}: Hey Paimon... You wanna hear a secret?
Paimon: Um... sure?
{NICKNAME}: Listen carefully...
Paimon: Mm-hmm?
{NICKNAME}: ...Zhongli is Rex Lapis.
Paimon: *gasp* What a crazy twist! Why would you spoil— Wait a second, we figured out that one ages ago!
voices.title: About the Big No-No of Detective Novels...

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: Pro tip. While we're in Fontaine, if someone ever picks a fight with you, you should never fight back unless there are witnesses around.
Paimon: Huh? Why's that?
{NICKNAME}: 'Cause without any evidence, the court'll probably reject your claim of self-defense, and they'll just rule that it was an intentional street fight.
Paimon: Okay, and then what?
{NICKNAME}: Well if that happens, you'll almost certainly end up having to duel before you're put to trial.
{NICKNAME}: At that point, you'll either have to fight the same person all over again, or go head-to-head with their Champion Duelist.
Paimon: ...Paimon just feels bad for whoever has to fight you.
voices.title: About Claiming Self-Defense...

voices.text:
Paimon: Pretty crazy how things that happened only yesterday show up in today's issue of The Steambird...
Paimon: Even stuff that happened late at night way outside the city makes it in. How do they manage to get these articles written up so quickly?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, not to mention printed first thing in the morning.
Paimon: Hehe, Paimon gets it! There must be a magic printer at The Steambird's office. As soon as the reporters bring in the latest news, they feed it to the printer, and it goes om-nom-nom-nom-nom, gobbling all the writing up ready to spit it back out when it's printing time!
Paimon: They probably have some reporters bursting in through the doors at the last minute, yelling "WAIT! There's one last article to feed to the printer!"
{NICKNAME}: That's definitely a very compelling image. But as far as I know, magic printers like that don't exist — it's all thanks to the tireless work of the editing team that The Steambird gets printed on time every day. They sit there going "Huh? Hmph! Uhh... Oh no!" as they race through correcting spelling errors, then they squeeeeeeeze it all into neat vertical columns of text, and run to their colleagues shouting "Just give me five more minutes, please!" That's the real magic behind meeting publishing deadlines.
Paimon: Whoa... It's pretty amazing that they're able to make a whole newspaper in just one day. Do they ever get time to sleep?
voices.title: About The Steambird's Editors...

voices.text:
Paimon: Huh, novels in Fontaine have weirdly long names. This one's called "Do Clockwork Meka Dream of Cogwheel Chiropractors?"
Paimon: But the writing style and themes are pretty different from Inazuma's light novels.
{NICKNAME}: According to the synopsis, this novel is about a clockwork meka experiencing back pain due to bending over for extended periods. It finally gives in, quits its job as an illustrator, then goes on a long journey looking for a chiropractor to cure its mechanical spine...
Paimon: That actually sounds pretty interesting.
{NICKNAME}: But why a chiropractor, though? Wouldn't an engineer do the job better? They could just go to the Fontaine Research Institute, and save themselves the long journey.
Paimon: Well yeah, but... Having met some of the engineers from the institute, Paimon can see why they wouldn't want to...
{NICKNAME}: Oh yeah, that's true. But anyway, even though the protagonist of the story is a clockwork meka, you can still tell that it was written by a human. Imagine if they got a real clockwork meka to write a novel... I wonder what they'd write about?
Paimon: Hmm... How about this: "I Awoke One Morning and Found Myself Human!"
{NICKNAME}: Hey, that's a good one, Paimon.
voices.title: About Fontaine's Novels...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Opera Epiclese is used for both criminal trials and performances, so... wait...
{NICKNAME}: Hmm? What's bothering you, Paimon?
Paimon: Well, what if someone did a show about a criminal trial there? How would the audience be able to tell whether it's a real trial or not?
{NICKNAME}: That's a very good question. Can you imagine the looks that the actor playing the criminal would get out on the street the following day? Everyone who recognized them would say "Hey! Weren't you the one on trial yesterday!?"
Paimon: Yeah, exactly! It would get sooo confusing!
{NICKNAME}: The actor would constantly be telling everyone: "It was just a show, for goodness' sake! Stop treating it like it's real!"
Paimon: Hmph, well they'd only have themselves to blame. What do they expect, staging a show about a trial in the Opera Epiclese? Clearly they're just trying to confuse people. What a terrible idea.
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, it is a terrible idea. What were you thinking, Paimon!?
Paimon: Wait, what? Nothing! Just... what a terrible idea it would be if... someone... came up with that idea...
voices.title: About Trials and Shows...

voices.text:
Paimon: Fonta tastes amazing, don't you think?
{NICKNAME}: Yep. It's so refreshing, especially when you down the whole thing in one big gulp.
Paimon: Can you buy a glass for Paimon? Paimon's always wanted to try that thing.
{NICKNAME}: What thing?
Paimon: Just buy it, you'll see in a minute!
Paimon: Glug glug glug glug...
Paimon: Ahhhhh.
Paimon: That's what those drunkards do after they clink their glasses together. Paimon's been itching to try it for ages!
{NICKNAME}: Don't imitate them, Paimon... It's not a good look on you.
voices.title: About Fonta...

voices.text:
Paimon: Gardemeks carry out whatever task they're programmed to do. So basically, they can do whatever you tell them to!
{NICKNAME}: Got another bright idea, Paimon?
Paimon: Yep! Paimon needs a commission-handling Gardemek, a material-harvesting Gardemek, and a domain-exploring Gardemek...
Paimon: Ooh, and a gourmet-chef Gardemek, too! Then we can sit back and enjoy our new, fully automated lifestyle!
{NICKNAME}: They're extremely expensive to own and operate, though. And don't forget there's maintenance and repair costs as well.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, lemme do some quick napkin-math here... Using a Gardemek, the average cost to harvest a single Mint would come to around 6,300 Mora...
Paimon: What!? That's eye wateringly expensive...
Paimon: ...Suddenly, Paimon feels like we adventurers don't get paid enough for the high-value work we do!
voices.title: About Gardemeks...

voices.text:
Paimon: Fontaine's underwater world is so pretty! There's so many kinds of fish that Paimon's never seen before.
{NICKNAME}: If only we could swim underwater in other places too.
Paimon: Yeah, it's a real shame...
Paimon: If you could go diving anywhere you wanted, where would you choose?
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... Probably... either Liyue Harbor or Guyun Stone Forest.
Paimon: Ooh, great idea! There's gotta be some sunken ships around there full of treasure! We could make a fortune!
{NICKNAME}: Ooh, there's also Sangonomiya Shrine in Inazuma. The view underwater must be stunning around there. So, what about you, Paimon? Where would you go?
Paimon: Let Paimon think... Well, since you already chose places in Liyue and Inazuma, Paimon's gonna go for... Cider Lake!
{NICKNAME}: Not a bad choice. But you gotta be careful, because just when you're swimming along, minding your own business...
Paimon: Y—Yeah?
{NICKNAME}: Suddenly, you notice something slowly sinking in front of you...
Paimon: Huh!?
{NICKNAME}: It's round and chubby, with a red-and-white pattern on its surface. The moment you realize what it is, you know it's already too late...
Paimon: A Jumpy Dumpty!
{NICKNAME}: BOOM!
Paimon: Waaaaaah! And Paimon goes flying into the sky!
voices.title: About Diving...

voices.text:
Paimon: There seems to be a lot of eccentric artists in the Court of Fontaine. Apparently, they often stage artistic performances at the opera house, too.
Paimon: The people of Fontaine sure place a lot of importance on the arts. Guess that's why they call it the "City of the Arts"!
Paimon: It's nothing like Sumeru, where people had to do their performances in secret...
{NICKNAME}: You're pretty into the arts, huh?
Paimon: Of course! Paimon's pretty much a connoisseur.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, so what makes something "art" in your opinion?
Paimon: Well... Art should be something that's out of the ordinary. Something that sparkles like the stars at night!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... By that definition, I have a work of art following me around wherever I go.
Paimon: ...Huh?
Paimon: Wait... You don't mean Paimon, do you?
{NICKNAME}: Yup! And now that I think about it, you should consider doing a performance some time. Paimon, live at the opera house... I bet a lot of people would go to see that.
Paimon: No way! Not gonna happen!
voices.title: About Art...

voices.text:
Paimon: You know what's strange? Clockwork meka are extremely intricate, and yet people regularly manage to fix them just by whacking them a few times. How does that work?
{NICKNAME}: I guess if a gear or drive shaft comes loose, sometimes whacking it or giving it a shake is enough to make the parts latch back on to each other.
Paimon: Huh? Paimon didn't follow that...
{NICKNAME}: Well, simply put, if the meka isn't actually broken, a little tap can nudge the parts back into the right places.
{NICKNAME}: But on the other hand, if one of the parts is damaged, then no amount of whacking is ever gonna fix it.
Paimon: Ohh! So it's like knocking sense into people. It works fine as long as they've got a brain, and they're just having a dumb moment. But if they're a total airhead, there's nowhere for the sense to go!
Paimon: ...Wait, why are you staring at Paimon's forehead?
{NICKNAME}: Don't worry, I'm not gonna whack you in the head. It wouldn't work anyway.
Paimon: Phew, well that's a relief— Wait... Hey!
voices.title: About Fixing Malfunctions...

voices.text:
Paimon: So there's this place in Fontaine called the Fortress of Meropide. Was it named after someone called Meropide?
{NICKNAME}: I've never heard anything about that, but you could be right.
Paimon: Paimon's kinda envious. Having a building named after you must be an amazing feeling... When you have the time, can you build something in your Serenitea Pot and name it "the Fortress of Paimon"?
{NICKNAME}: Sure. In fact, I can do one better — I'll build it in downtown Fontaine.
Paimon: Really? But surely that'd be way too expensive. Are you sure you can afford it?
{NICKNAME}: Oh, absolutely. It won't actually cost that much.
Paimon: Wow, you're so generous! So, what're you gonna build...?
{NICKNAME}: I was thinking a cozy little clay... bungalow, with a wood-burner for under-floor heating, a waterbed... a few chopped onions, salt and pepper, some greens... and, um...
Paimon: Hey! Ugh, you are unbelievable! Can't we get through one nation without you cracking this stupid joke!?
voices.title: About the Fortress of Meropide...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon's heard that the earliest clockwork components ever invented actually work on a very simple principle!
Paimon: You take a long object made from a durable material, bend it, and wait for it to return to its original shape. As it rebounds, you can use the energy it gives off to power gears and stuff, and then you basically have an engine!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... A long object made from a durable material... *gasp* You know what that reminds me of?
{NICKNAME}: Cryo and Pyro Regisvines! Don't you think?
Paimon: Eek! Of all the things you could've thought of, why those two?
Paimon: Huh, but come to think of it, the regisvines are pretty good at whipping their stalks around...
{NICKNAME}: And they're really strong too. If you let them charge up their energy and swing at you...
{NICKNAME}: They'll knock down anyone in their path. Even me — and we both know how strong I am!
Paimon: So are you saying that... you could turn the Regisvines into a clockwork mechanism?
{NICKNAME}: Well, think about it. Since Cryo and Pyro lifeforms are highly incompatible, if we put them both next to each other at a slight incline, so their necks are tilted towards one another...
{NICKNAME}: They'd spin non-stop to avoid touching each other!
{NICKNAME}: It would be the world's most powerful clockwork mechanism! Once we found a way to harness it, it would generate enough energy to power most of the machines in Fontaine!
Paimon: Ohhh! Yeah, you're right!
Paimon: This is a genius idea! Eat your heart out, Fontaine Research Institute!
Paimon: All we need to do now is find a way to bring the Regisvines to Fontaine, put them in position, and...
Paimon: Wait a sec... How the heck are we gonna get those overgrown ferns to Fontaine?
{NICKNAME}: As soon as we've tackled the minor issues of practicality and cost-effectiveness...
{NICKNAME}: ...How about we explore the details ahead of us later?
voices.title: About Supermeka...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon thought we'd be saying goodbye to the amazing cafés after we left Sumeru. But it seems like people in Fontaine are big coffee drinkers too!
{NICKNAME}: They sure are. Even the newspapers run articles about how great coffee is at keeping you awake and alert. And at boosting your energy levels, so you can keep performing at peak efficiency during a long working day.
Paimon: Whew, any job where you need coffee to stay energized must be exhausting...
Paimon: Like, umm... Blacksmiths? Maybe chefs too... And adventurers — they're always running around all over the place. Hey, and what about divers?
{NICKNAME}: Divers, huh? That's definitely the odd one out here...
{NICKNAME}: How are divers supposed to drink coffee when they work underwater the entire time?
Paimon: Yeah, that's a good question!
Paimon: They can't take off their helmets underwater, so they'd probably have to shut themselves inside an even bigger glass box and drain all the water out before they could finally drink their coffee. Probably from a bottle...
Paimon: No, wait... If the coffee's already in a bottle, all they'd need is a long straw that goes from the bottle into their helmet. Then they'd be able to take a sip of coffee whenever they want!
{NICKNAME}: Hehe, eww, haha. But then the coffee would go cold!
{NICKNAME}: Cold coffee is just gross. With the important exception of iced coffee, but that's its own thing.
Paimon: Well that's no problem. They can just bring a stove with them underwater.
Paimon: You've seen the kind of stove that most people use in Fontaine, right? It only has one small opening up at the top. As long as that's sealed nice and tight, it won't go out even underwater!
Paimon: Wait a second... No way, is that... That's it! That must be the whole reason stoves in Fontaine are made that way!
{NICKNAME}: Ding ding ding, right answer! That is indeed the reason behind the design of the Fontaine-style stove.
Paimon: Hehe, Paimon's the smartest!
Paimon: Hey, how about we open an underwater café? Paimon bets there's lots of divers out there craving some coffee while they're down in the depths... Yeah, this could be a huge opportunity for us!
Paimon: Once we open the world's first-ever underwater café, the Mora will come rolling in! Heck, and why stop at cafés? The ocean's our oyster! We could build a whole shopping mall down there! Then a whole underwater business district...
Paimon: Hee-hee! Ah, it's gotta be the best feeling in the world, making Mora through your very own stroke of business genius!
{NICKNAME}: Just one thing, okay? ...Don't go taking out a loan in my name!
voices.title: About Underwater Cafés...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Steambird's head office is in Fontaine, right? Paimon wonders what stories make it into their newspapers.
Paimon: Do you think they reported on our adventures with Dvalin? Or our duel with the Raiden Shogun? Oh, and everything that happened at the Akademiya!
{NICKNAME}: I'm sure they cover just about everything that goes on. It's more a question of where it would appear — they probably have different sections reserved for different topics.
Paimon: Ooh, well in that case, we must make it onto the front page all the time! Surely that's where all the most exciting stories go.
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... I'm not so sure. We might've made front-page news once or twice, I guess. But I wouldn't be surprised if the headlines mostly focus on hit new operas or well-known actors.
{NICKNAME}: You know, stuff like, "Actor X Spotted Drinking Coffee on Street," "Actor Y Goes Public About New Relationship," or "Actor Z to Retire From Performing."
Paimon: Why would they fill the best page with stuff like that? It's completely pointless.
{NICKNAME}: Well... trivial, maybe, but not pointless. Those are the stories that grab people's attention and convince them to buy the paper to get all the details.
Paimon: *sigh* ...Fine. Well... Maybe we'll be on the first few pages then? Surely, they've gotta put some real news in there. And it's gotta be interesting enough to keep people reading after they've gotten their dose of celebrity gossip. Right?
{NICKNAME}: The first few pages cover positive local news stories in the Court of Fontaine. Things like food and commodity prices going down, or progress updates on the aquabus expansions.
{NICKNAME}: They put these reports at the most prominent locations inside the newspaper. The point of them is mostly just to kill time.
{NICKNAME}: What goes on at the Akademiya might be important, but it doesn't directly impact the lives of people in Fontaine.
Paimon: Huh... So, where would they put our stories then?
{NICKNAME}: I'd guess on the very back page, after everything else.
Paimon: Aww... Why so far back!?
{NICKNAME}: I think they call it... "saving the best till last."
{NICKNAME}: The editors probably embellish things a lot to flesh the story out, then break it into several chunks to make it into a series that runs over several days.
Paimon: Alright, so... what's the "point" of the final page, then?
{NICKNAME}: It gives the newspaper its "raison d'etre."
voices.title: About The Steambird...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon was not expecting to see clockwork meka dancing... As dangerous as it is to get too close to them, it sure is nice to watch them from a distance.
Paimon: Hehe, imagine if they had ones that could sing and play musical instruments, too. That'd be really cool!
{NICKNAME}: Then you'd just need some meka for the audience, and you'd have a show by meka, for meka.
Paimon: Uhhh... Somehow, that's a pretty scary thought...
Paimon: Anyway, meka are meant to do stuff, not sit there and watch a show... Ooh! How about meka that can paint? Paimon bets their paintings would look just like photos taken with a Kamera.
{NICKNAME}: Sounds like you could just use a Kamera.
Paimon: Oh, right, yeah... Hmm...
Paimon: Ugh, Paimon's brain's stopped working. What about you? If you could make a clockwork meka do anything at all, what would it be?
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... Travel guiding, perhaps.
{NICKNAME}: Bleep-blorp. This is your guidebot speaking. Please go straight on at the next crossroads. Bloop-blerp.
Paimon: Uh, P—Paimon's just remembered how much training you need before you can own a clockwork meka! And how expensive they are! Also, who knows if they even work outside of Fontaine, heh...
Paimon: The best travel guide in Teyvat will not lose her job to some machine! At least... at least not yet!
voices.title: About Clockwork Meka...

voices.text:
Paimon: There always seems to be people throwing Mora into the fountain on Erinnyes.
{NICKNAME}: Yeah. Supposedly, the fountain fairies listen to people's wishes. That's probably how the custom began.
Paimon: Huh? So even fountain fairies need Mora?
Paimon: Whoa, they must be living the dream! All they need to do is find a fountain to live in, and they're all set! No need to work, just sit back and wait for people to literally throw Mora to you.
{NICKNAME}: I don't think that's quite how it works... You have to grant wishes, remember?
Paimon: Oh, okay, well... "Oh young traveler, your wishes have been heard. Which lost sword is it that you seek? The Dull Blade, or the Silver Sword?"
{NICKNAME}: They both look like trash, to be honest.
Paimon: Just choose one.
{NICKNAME}: "Oh fair maiden of the fountain, neither of these swords is mine, and neither do I desire, for what I seek is my lost travel companion."
Paimon: Huh? You... You are a sneaky one, young traveler... Okay then, the fountain fairy shall grant your wish and become your best travel companion ever!
voices.title: About Fountains...

voices.text:
Paimon: Operas in Fontaine come in so many different genres. Historical, myths and legends, even fairytales and modern romances...
{NICKNAME}: And lots of adventure stories too.
Paimon: Oh yeah, like "Tancrede et Chariclea"! Oh Tancrede, you fool! If only you'd recognized Chariclea before it was too late...
{NICKNAME}: Apparently, the story's based on true events.
Paimon: Ooh... Does that mean that there'll be opera adaptations of our adventures one day?
Paimon: We've been through so many adventures together. There's gotta be a scriptwriter out there who's interested in taking our story to the stage!
Paimon: And they won't have to worry about crafting the perfect tragedy, either. Everyone loves a happy ending, right?
{NICKNAME}: Ooh, how about we get a head start and assign voices to ourselves?
Paimon: Hmm... Paimon thinks you have a mezzo-soprano voice. What do you think Paimon should be?
{NICKNAME}: Remind me — what's that shrill voice that most prima donnas have?
Paimon: Oh, you must be thinking of coloratura soprano— Hey!
voices.title: About Opera...

voices.text:
Paimon: Apparently, every Melusine gets their own special token when they're born. They treat it as a symbol of their very being.
{NICKNAME}: If you were a Melusine, what would your token be?
Paimon: Definitely a fork! To represent Paimon's lifelong mission to taste all the delicious food in the whole world!
{NICKNAME}: Not Mora, then?
Paimon: Ooh, good point... Yeah, if it were Mora, it'd mean that Paimon's destined to be a super rich person. Then Paimon could buy anything she wants!
Paimon: Hmmmmm... Argh, Paimon's so torn! Both are so tempting...
{NICKNAME}: How about a fork made from Mora? Then you can have your cake and eat it, so to speak.
Paimon: Wow, that's a great idea!
Paimon: Anyway, enough about Paimon. Your token would probably be... a cooking pot, to represent being Paimon's personal gourmet chef!
{NICKNAME}: No no no, my token would be Paimon.
Paimon: Aw, really?
{NICKNAME}: With Paimon as my token, everything that you have would ultimately belong to me.
Paimon: Uh... Okay sure. Friends share everything, right?
{NICKNAME}: Haha, yeah... My stuff would still be mine...
Paimon: Hey, no fair!
voices.title: About Melusines...

voices.text:
Paimon: People in the city keep telling us how Palais Mermonia is a suuuper stressful place to work.
Paimon: But when we went to see it for ourselves, it seemed like hardly anyone works there, and the few people who do work there were hardly working.
Paimon: In fact, they looked like they didn't have a care in the world... What part of working there is supposed to be so stressful, exactly?
{NICKNAME}: Maybe the work they carry out is essential, but insignificant.
Paimon: How can something be both of those things at the same time?
{NICKNAME}: Well... Okay, so imagine that one day, you suddenly forgot how to fly and fell to the ground...
Paimon: That'll never happen. Flying's a piece of cake for Paimon.
{NICKNAME}: Probably not — but just in case, we should make sure that there's a cart loaded with cushions ready to catch you at all times.
{NICKNAME}: The cart would have to be designed to withstand any environment and weather conditions, and the cushions would need to be soft enough to break your fall gently...
{NICKNAME}: It would need to be built from the sturdiest timber and strongest rope, and packed with plenty of medical supplies and snacks...
{NICKNAME}: And all because keeping Paimon safe and sound is absolutely essential.
Paimon: You really mean that? Aw, thanks, hehe... But there's really no need to go to all that trouble.
Paimon: Paimon's been flying for a really long time. There's no way Paimon's gonna suddenly drop out of the air. So you don't need to worry about it.
{NICKNAME}: See? That's why it's insignificant.
{NICKNAME}: If it ever did happen, the consequences would be disastrous — hence why it's essential to be prepared.
{NICKNAME}: But practically speaking, the chances of it happening are next to nothing. So it's insignificant at the same time.
{NICKNAME}: If someone in the Palais Mermonia was assigned a task like that, it'd be up to them to decide how busy they wanna get. Chances are, they'd probably just sit back and do nothing.
Paimon: But... What if Paimon really does forget how to fly one day? What's gonna happen when Paimon falls to the ground?
{NICKNAME}: I'll be here to catch you, no matter what. Because you're not "essential but insignificant" — you're the best travel companion ever!
voices.title: About the Palais Mermonia...

voices.text:
Paimon: Hey, so the valleys here are just bursting with shiny gemstones!
Paimon: This could be a huge opportunity for us! We should get digging ASAP. With any luck, we'll hit the jackpot and we'll never have to worry about Mora again!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... But how would you actually know when you've hit the jackpot? Can you even tell which stones are the valuable ones?
Paimon: Uhh, well... Paimon just figured... the shinier the stone, the more valuable it is! Yeah, that should be about right!
{NICKNAME}: You're starting to sound like an evil fairytale dragon, hoarding all the shinies they can get their greedy claws on...
Paimon: Hehe, except we're in Natlan now — so instead of "evil dragon," it's "noble Saurian"!
Paimon: "O brave and cunning {NICKNAME}, follow this noble Saurian, for she shall lead you to the most precious gemstone in the entire world!"
{NICKNAME}: Great! Except she can't tell which stones are the valuable ones, so how's that gonna work?
voices.title: About the Children of Echoes' Gems...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Scions of the Canopy sure do love their extreme outdoor sports. Seems like they have a real appetite for danger.
Paimon: Free solo climbing, skysurfing, volcano parkour, bungee jumping off cliffs... Whew, even the thought of it makes Paimon light-headed!
{NICKNAME}: Really? Honestly, some of the stuff we've done is at least as dangerous as that... We froze half to death on Dragonspine, narrowly avoided being fried in all those thunderstorms, got sandblasted in the scorching desert, stared death in the face in those eerie Withering Zones... The list goes on.
Paimon: Huh, when you put it like that... Yeah, we've been through some pretty extreme stuff.
{NICKNAME}: Mhm, but we're built different. Most people's idea of "danger" is probably just an average day on the road for us. That's probably how it is for the Scions of the Canopy with their extreme sports as well.
Paimon: Whoa, wait a second! Let's get one thing straight: YOU might be built different, but Paimon sure as heck isn't.
Paimon: Now, Paimon's sure you and your danger-braving buddies know what you're doing, but the second we find ourselves in serious trouble, Paimon's gonna... hide behind you until it's over.
voices.title: About the Scions of the Canopy...

voices.text:
Paimon: The People of the Springs are so chill. If they're not relaxing in a hot spring, they're planning their next big soak...
{NICKNAME}: Apparently, some of them even hire musicians to play some relaxing music while they take a dip. The warm water relaxes the body, and the soothing music relaxes the mind...
Paimon: Whoa, that sounds so nice, Paimon wants to try it for herself...
{NICKNAME}: Alright. Well, next time you visit the hot springs, I'll play some Aranara music for you.
Paimon: Ooh~ ...Um, but Paimon doesn't play any instruments, so what happens when it's your turn to go in the spring?
{NICKNAME}: You can sing me a song. Maybe... an opera from Fontaine?
Paimon: That's way too hard! Also — not exactly relaxing! That kind of music will put your blood pressure through the roof!
Paimon: How about some Natlan rap instead? Paimon's been practicing, check this out:
Paimon: "Hey! Flyin' in your face, it's Paimon the guide, no stranger to danger, takes it in her stride..."
Paimon: "Saw a beast called blubber in the nation of water, my Guhua brother got his weapons in order, sword in one hand and a spear in the other..."
{NICKNAME}: Wow, very smooth!
{NICKNAME}: If I was listening to that in a hot spring, I'd be tapping the water to the beat like a drum.
Paimon: Yeah, it'd be like a big music festival! And anyone who's late to the party, the rhythm of the water would get them right into the groove!
{NICKNAME}: Uhhh... Wait, didn't we start this by saying how the hot springs are meant to be relaxing?
voices.title: About the Hot Springs of Natlan...

voices.text:
Paimon: Don't you think those masked warriors look super cool?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, really gives them an air of mystery.
Paimon: Right!? Don't you think Paimon should get in on this too? Put on a mask and win some wrestling matches with the Collective of Plenty? She could make a whole new name for herself!
Paimon: Paimon's even thought of some catchphrases, get this: "A saurian warrior never removes her mask!"
Paimon: Famous adventurer by day, mighty saurian warrior by night. Does that sound cool or what!?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, it does, but there's just one problem...
Paimon: Hmm? What's that?
{NICKNAME}: You'll just look like Paimon in a mask. No air of mystery there.
voices.title: About the Collective of Plenty...

voices.text:
Paimon: Here in Natlan, they seem to use woven scrolls where most nations would use books. It feels so different reading off of them.
{NICKNAME}: Yeah. They say it started with the Masters of the Night-Wind, when the Shamans began recording their tribal history and legends on woven material. As the practice became more widely adopted, the number and variety of stories grew.
Paimon: Ooh, Paimon should make a record of all our adventures as well! That way, if you ever start a tribe called the Travelers, you'll have your very own historical record!
Paimon: Plus, it could make a really cool cape. And an extra blanket when you're camping in the wild...
{NICKNAME}: That would make for one "weathered" chronicle.
voices.title: About Woven Goods...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon's heard that everyone from the Collective of Plenty is built like a bricklayer!
{NICKNAME}: Maybe you should go stay with them for a while. Grow those muscles out.
Paimon: No! Paimon likes herself the way she is now.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, then what about staying with the Flower-Feather Clan instead? Their thing is flying. I bet they could help you sharpen your skills!
Paimon: Huh? But... isn't Paimon good enough at flying already?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, but then you'd be able to carry me when you fly.
Paimon: Nope, not happening! How would that even be possible?
{NICKNAME}: Well, if you had those muscles I talked about...
Paimon: Oh, geez, not this again... For the last time, no!
voices.title: About the Collective of Plenty and the Flower-Feather Clan...

voices.text:
Paimon: Oooh, there are so many cute Saurians in Natlan! Paimon's gonna make friends with every single one!
{NICKNAME}: Oh? Someone sounds confident...
Paimon: You bet! Paimon's got it all figured out!
{NICKNAME}: Oh you do, huh? Come on then, what's the secret to making Saurian friends?
Paimon: It's really simple! First, you've gotta sweet-talk them, show 'em you mean well so they relax their defenses. Then, you gently pat them on the head — that makes them feel more comfortable around you.
Paimon: Last but not least: Get 'em some good grub! The way to a Saurian's heart is through the stomach, after all! What do you think? Solid plan, huh?
{NICKNAME}: Hmm, what do I think... I think that all of these tactics would also work really well on you, Paimon.
Paimon: Would not! Paimon can't be won over by some cheap tricks!
{NICKNAME}: Huh? Oh, you misunderstand! I meant to say that you're as cute as a baby Saurian!
Paimon: Hah! Flattery, really? You think that'll work on Paimon? Think again!
{NICKNAME}: But I was being sincere, Paimon! Ah, how can I prove it to you? With some Sweet Madame, perhaps?
Paimon: ...Wait, really? Sweet Madame? Oh, heck yes! Paimon could totally go for some of that right now!
Paimon: ...Uhh... What's with that smug look on your face? ...What!? Is Paimon missing something?
voices.title: About Ways to Make Friends With Saurians...

voices.text:
Paimon: Word is that speed's of the essence when doing archaeology work with the Children of Echoes. Why's that?
{NICKNAME}: It's probably because this place is absolutely overflowing with relics...
Paimon: Uh, but isn't that a good thing?
{NICKNAME}: Well, more relics means more competition! Imagine you saw a really cool stone slate one day, and planned to come back and grab it the day after — only to show up the next day and find someone else had already beaten you to it!
Paimon: Um, Paimon still doesn't get it...
{NICKNAME}: Okay, here's another analogy: Imagine one night you're all ready to dig in to a delicious snack... but then you find a piece of it's missing!
Paimon: Ahh! Yeah, that'd be terrible!
Paimon: ...Wait a sec, that's exactly what happened last night... Anything you wanna confess, {NICKNAME}?
voices.title: About Archaeology...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon's heard that even in Natlan, there are lots of ways to resolve conflict that don't involve contests of strength.
{NICKNAME}: Really? In the Nation of War?
Paimon: Yeah! Like, apparently, some people in the Children of Echoes settle their disputes by holding a dance-off!
{NICKNAME}: A dance-off? So, they mutually decide on a time and place...
Paimon: Uh-huh!
{NICKNAME}: And just dance their socks off?
Paimon: Mm-hmm!
{NICKNAME}: Until one person gets so exhausted, they can't get up anymore?
Paimon: Yep!
Paimon: ...Wait, what the... Hold on, that IS a contest of strength!
voices.title: About Resolving Conflicts...

voices.text:
Paimon: Guess what? Paimon just thought of the best Mora-making idea ever!
{NICKNAME}: Oh? Do tell.
Paimon: Just look at how many people pass by this place every day. If we opened a business here, right outside the Stadium, we'd make a fortune without even trying!
{NICKNAME}: So... What would you sell?
Paimon: Uhhh... maybe... alchemical potions from Mondstadt?
{NICKNAME}: I think there's already people selling similar stuff...
Paimon: In that case, ummm... Ooh! Ores from Liyue! Yeah, we could make a killing off of those!
{NICKNAME}: Pretty sure the Children of Echoes are already in that business, too...
Paimon: Yeah... Wait, Paimon's got it — rugs from Sumeru! Those'll definitely be a hit!
{NICKNAME}: Unfortunately, that's the specialty of the Masters of the Night-Wind.
Paimon: Well then... we'll fence the whole Stadium up! And charge an admission fee to everyone who tries to get inside, whether they're a contestant or a spectator!
{NICKNAME}: You'll be locked up before your fence is even half-finished...
Paimon: Grrrrrrrr! Why does getting rich have to be so hard?
voices.title: About Ways to Make a Fortune...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon will never forget the first saurians we saw in Natlan. They're just fascinating creatures.
Paimon: There was the Tepetlisaurs with their bouncy heads, the Koholasaurs with their smooth backs, and then the Yumkasaurs with their fluffy ears and heads.
{NICKNAME}: I bet a baby Yumkasaur would make the best teddy bear...
Paimon: Yeah... Hey, their fur probably keeps growing out as they get older, right? Do you think it starts getting in the way eventually?
Paimon: Like, imagine if a Yumkasaur had really long fur around the ears and head... they'd barely be able to see where they're going. And that could be kinda dangerous...
{NICKNAME}: You seem to have thought a lot about this. Are you planning on becoming a saurian hairstylist?
Paimon: Uh... Are you serious?
{NICKNAME}: Just think about it. Once you get famous, you'll be rolling in Mora!
Paimon: Oh... You're right! This is it, this is how Paimon makes her fortune!
Paimon: Paimon's gonna become the hairstylist for every Yumkasaur in Natlan! Hehehe, so much Mora...
Paimon: No, wait, the Mora's secondary! The best part of this plan is making friends with all the Yumkasaurs! Life will be sooo happy!
{NICKNAME}: But they're big, you know. It's gotta take a long time to style all that fur with just an ordinary pair of scissors. You might find you can only take one customer per day...
{NICKNAME}: If you're serious about this stylist business, you'd better start building some strength! At the very least, aim to lift a pair of scissors as big as the Dull Blade!
Paimon: The Dull Blade? But isn't that your weapon?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, but I can let you borrow it for training. Come on! Let's get practicing!
Paimon: Hey... This isn't "training," this is "give Paimon the sword and let her fight the monsters instead"! Paimon did not sign up for this!
voices.title: About Saurian Stylists...

voices.text:
Paimon: So in Natlan, warriors who impress the Wayob enough get an Ancient Name. Paimon's so jealous! Having an Ancient Name would be so cool!
{NICKNAME}: Huh? Don't you already have a bucket load of titles, Paimon?
Paimon: Hmm? Oh wait... Yeah, you're right!
Paimon: Paimon's your "best travel companion" and "trusty guide," plus she's the "Trendy Flyer," "Silver Companion," and "Assistant to the Honorary Senior Researcher"... Heck yeah, Paimon's an actual legend!
Paimon: If the people of Natlan end up making a record of our adventures, Paimon's gonna make sure they use every single one of those titles!
{NICKNAME}: Huh? But wouldn't that make everything too long?
{NICKNAME}: Just think about it. If the locals also used all of their names, records would look something like:
{NICKNAME}: On this day, "Uthabiti" Kachina of the Children of Echoes, otherwise known as the Nanatzcayans, and "Umoja" Mualani of the People of the Springs, of Meztli fame, encountered "Malipo" Kinich of the Scions of the Canopy of Huitztlan, traveling alongside his impish partner, K'uhul Ajaw, while on their way to the Masters of the Night-Wind in Mictlan...
Paimon: Okay, okay, you can stop now! Geez, with a document that long, it'd stretch from here to the Stadium and back... and that's before it even got to the point!
Paimon: Well, if Paimon had to pick just one out of all her titles... Yep, it'd have to be: "Best companion ever"!
voices.title: About Ancient Names...

voices.text:
Paimon: So just between the two of us... Paimon's been wondering about something. It's to do with the competitions at the Stadium.
Paimon: You know how there's a point system? First everyone fights in teams, then for the teams that make it through, there's a set number of one-on-one matches, and after that, everyone's ranked based on their final scores.
Paimon: Why did they structure it like that?
{NICKNAME}: Maybe it's to maintain suspense until the final round? Everyone loves to see the underdog make a comeback at the last minute.
Paimon: Could be, could be... Or maybe it's because they wanna avoid a situation where there's only two contestants and they're evenly matched?
{NICKNAME}: Yeah... They'd end up having to call it a draw and quit.
Paimon: Exactly! It'd be like pitting the most aggressive Tatankasaur against the most slippery Yumkasaur. Tatankasaur attacks, Yumkasaur dodges, and so on and so forth, until a whole day and night has passed...
Paimon: By this point, the audience is starving, so they end the fight and agree to a round two some other time.
Paimon: But round two comes and goes, and there's still no clear winner. This time, the fight only ends because the Yumkasaur makes an illegal surprise attack and injures the Tatankasaur.
Paimon: ...Before long, we've ended up with "Tatanka vs. Yumka," "Tatanka vs. Yumka 2," "Tatanka vs. Yumka: Return of the Sacred Scales," "Tatanka vs. Yumka: Over the Volcano"... and the sequels show no signs of stopping.
Paimon: ...Wait, we should totally get those made into a film series! We'd make a ton of Mora.
{NICKNAME}: Not a bad idea... Although, I don't think the Scions of the Canopy would be too happy about you making their Saurian the villain!
Paimon: Alright, well you pitch an idea then, if you're such a film critic!
voices.title: About the Stadium of the Sacred Flame...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Natlanese don't seem to leave Natlan much, do they?
{NICKNAME}: Nope, and there are some good reasons for that.
Paimon: Hmm... That must make things pretty difficult for anyone who wants to be an adventurer, huh?
Paimon: Think about it — if they can't go to other nations, they miss out on a ton of potential commissions. If they can't go exploring unknown ruins, surely they can't make a whole lot of Mora... It's too bad.
{NICKNAME}: You'd think so, wouldn't you? But in fact, they've found ways around it.
Paimon: Huh?
{NICKNAME}: I've heard of a group in the People of the Springs who call themselves "wayfinders." They have a wealth of knowledge about Natlan's geography and ancient ruins, so a lot of foreign adventurers hire them as guides when they visit.
{NICKNAME}: Of course, that means they get paid for each trip, regardless of whether their client actually finds the treasure. So in the long run, they might actually earn more than a traditional adventurer would.
Paimon: Wow, okay... But wait — if they know so much about Natlan's ancient ruins, why don't they just go find the treasure themselves?
{NICKNAME}: Well, here's the thing... What if there never was any treasure to begin with?
Paimon: Whoa... Okay, Paimon's gonna need a minute to let that sink in...
voices.title: About Natlan's Adventurers...

voices.text:
Paimon: The Natlanese seem to do a lot of doodling everywhere. Except they don't call it "doodling," do they? They call it, uh... flow-something?
{NICKNAME}: "Phlogiston engraving." But strictly speaking, that refers to the engraving of special stone tablets. What you're talking about is just regular graffiti.
{NICKNAME}: Take this one, for example. It basically just says, "You're in Nanatzcayan territory now! Children of Echoes for the win!"
Paimon: That's pretty fun! Now Paimon wants in. Shall we do some graffiti of our own?
{NICKNAME}: We sure can. But what do you think we should draw?
Paimon: Well that's easy — a portrait of the best travel guide in all of Teyvat! Now let's see... Ah, there! Put it right there on that cliff face.
{NICKNAME}: So you want me to do the honors, huh? Alright then, lemme think about this... Yep, first we need to capture that classic Paimon facial expression: seething with rage...
Paimon: Mhm-hmm— Wait, what!? Grr... You know what, forget it! Paimon has decided to find a professional Natlanese graffiti artist instead!
voices.title: About Graffiti...

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: The Natlanese seem to have a genuinely close relationship with their saurians.
Paimon: Yeah! They're true companions, just like us. Inseparable wherever they go!
{NICKNAME}: So... let's say there was a competition between you and the saurians. Who do you think would win the title of champion companion?
Paimon: Huh? What sort of a question is that!?
{NICKNAME}: I mean, the more I think about it, it's like... You can't burrow into the ground like the tepetlisaurs, and you don't fly as fast as the qucusaurs...
Paimon: H—Hey! Y—You're thinking about this all wrong! For starters, Paimon flies way faster than any tepetlisaur, and she's better than the qucusaurs at, uh... at picking out the tastiest Chicken-Mushroom Skewer from the grill!
{NICKNAME}: And most importantly of all, Paimon has been at my side longer than any saurian.
Paimon: Exactly! Let's not forget who's the best travel guide in all of Teyvat, hehe!
{NICKNAME}: Alright, my trusty companion, shall we set off on our next adventure?
Paimon: Um, actually, now that Paimon's mentioned it, she feels like her Chicken-Mushroom-Skewer-picking-out skills have gotten a little rusty... C'mon, you should cook up a few so Paimon can practice!
voices.title: About Saurian Companions...

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon's been dying to hear your thoughts about this... What is the deal with Ajaw? And don't say you haven't noticed.
{NICKNAME}: Noticed what?
Paimon: ...! Try everything! He's completely different from every other Saurian! For starters, he can talk — matter of fact, he never shuts up! Also, he's always hovering around Kinich instead of walking on the ground. Oh, and don't get Paimon started on those stupid sunglasses! Why would a Saurian wear sunglasses? It doesn't make any sense!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm...
Paimon: Why are you looking at Paimon like that...?
{NICKNAME}: It's just... You talk a lot too, and you fly, plus... didn't you get yourself a pair of silly-looking glasses in Fontaine?
Paimon: ...That is completely different!
Paimon: But anyway, there's a more glaring issue here... Ajaw is flat as a pancake! He's floating around looking like a little cardboard cutout, and no one in Natlan bats an eyelid! Don't you think that's strange?
{NICKNAME}: It's definitely unusual. Then again, maybe everyone's just used to it by now.
{NICKNAME}: Ultimately, it's nobody's business but Ajaw's, so if you want answers, you'd probably have to ask him.
Paimon: But would he even tell us the truth? Paimon gets the feeling he'd just make up a bunch of phony-baloney to get us off his case...
Paimon: *gasp* Or maybe... He'd be like, "Okay, if you really wanna know... I'll show you!" And then poof! He'd turn us into cardboard cutouts too!
{NICKNAME}: Heh... Cardboard-cutout Paimon, now that I would love to see, hehehe...
Paimon: Hey... Cut it out! Paimon doesn't wanna be flat as a pancake...
voices.title: About Ajaw...

voices.text:
Paimon: Have you noticed the... makeup that Natlanese people wear? Or body paint, or tattoos, or graffiti, or whatever it's called — anyway, it looks really cool!
{NICKNAME}: I have noticed! "Body paint" is right, although it's not just any old paint. Apparently, it contains phlogiston.
Paimon: Wow, really?
{NICKNAME}: Yep. If you're interested to try it out, I'm pretty sure they offer a body painting experience specially for tourists — but they just use normal paint for that.
Paimon: Ooh! Well, since we're here... why don't we try it? All part of the experience.
{NICKNAME}: Sure thing. You'll need to pick a color palette and a motif first though. Each tribe has its own style.
Paimon: Alright, Paimon chooses, uh... Paimon chooses... Ugh! They all look so cool! Choosing between them is impossible.
Paimon: Meh, choosing is losing! Paimon will take them all!
{NICKNAME}: Wow... Today I learned that Paimon is a maximalist... Well, I'm sure some people would say "less is more," but I say — you do you, Paimon!
Paimon: What are you talking about!? Paimon never said anything about using them all at once! She just wants options, so she can switch up her style every day!
{NICKNAME}: ...Oh. That's too bad... I woulda loved to see Paimon with an elaborate arm-tattoo...
Paimon: Stop! Nope! Stop it! No imagining Paimon with an arm-tattoo! Not allowed!
voices.title: About Natlan's Body Painting Practices...

voices.text:
Paimon: The people and saurians of Natlan have a great relationship, huh? They live together, fight together, even fly together...
{NICKNAME}: Just like us, right? Except you're too small to take me flying... It's just a shame you can't grow any bigger. Not for want of trying, of course — you do eat a lot of Chicken-Mushroom Skewers...
Paimon: Hmph... Let's not forget that saurians can't be your guide. Or your conversation partner.
{NICKNAME}: It's strange to think that there was once a time when humans and saurians were enemies. And now they co-exist peacefully. Must've taken a lot of work to get to where things are today.
Paimon: If Paimon was a saurian, all it would have taken is some tasty food.
{NICKNAME}: You say that, but... what if you demanded a hundred chicken skewers per day, and the humans couldn't provide that much?
Paimon: Umm... Paimon could probably settle for fifty a day...
{NICKNAME}: Or even better — maybe the humans could team up with you and you could go hunting together. Then there'd be enough meat for everyone to eat their fill!
Paimon: Uh-huh! Peace between species all starts with a full stomach!
voices.title: About Living With Saurians...

voices.text:
Paimon: That volcano is so huge, you can see it from anywhere in Natlan... Where do you think all that magma comes from, though?
{NICKNAME}: One legend holds that an enormous Pyro Dragon slumbers in the deepest depths of Natlan. Within the dragon's body dwells the world's first flame, burning eternally, and causing boils to form on the dragon's back. Every once in a while, these boils spew out fire, which takes the form of magma when it comes above ground.
Paimon: For real!? But... what happens if the dragon ever wakes up? Natlan will be doomed!
{NICKNAME}: Yep, and that's why the Pyro Archon gets the tribes to periodically join forces and go pacify the dragon, to make sure it stays asleep.
Paimon： ...Wait, what? No, that's to fight the Abyss! Isn't it?
{NICKNAME}： ...Well, not if this story from a woven scroll I bought on the street is to be believed.
Paimon: Ugh, Paimon knew it!
voices.title: About the Volcano...

voices.text:
Paimon: There once was a great knight who was cursed to spend the daylight hours looking like a shabby old drunkard.
Paimon: Only in the dead of night would he return to his true form: a mature, brave, and self-respecting knight.
{NICKNAME}: Is there a way to lift the curse?
Paimon: Only if someone is willing to show genuine, heartfelt respect to the knight.
{NICKNAME}: Alright, I can do that. Let the curse be lifted!
Paimon: Ta-da! The curse has been lifted. Now, Grand Master Varka can choose for himself whether to be an old drunk or a respected knight.
Paimon: And then he said, "I'm sorry, but I've been a shabby old drunk all along." So now he's a shabby old drunk both day and night.
{NICKNAME}: Wait, that's terrible!
Paimon: There's a different version of the story in Natlan that goes like this: There once was a young girl cursed to become a snobby, stuck-up old lady during the day, only turning back into an innocent girl during the night.
Paimon: And, um... the only way to lift the curse was, uhh... having conversations about topics she liked.
{NICKNAME}: Well, I can already guess where this is going. If this was Madam Faruzan, then once the curse gets lifted, she'd probably say something like, "Hmph, and what's wrong with being old? Do you have a problem with that, young lady?"
Paimon: Right! And if it was Citlali...
{NICKNAME}: She'd get all anxious and pouty, and say, "But... but I've been an innocent young girl all along..."
Paimon: ...There's no actual curse in either of these stories, is there?
voices.title: About the Curse of the Night...

voices.text:
Paimon: Five hundred... One thousand... One thousand two hundred...
{NICKNAME}: What are you up to, Paimon?
Paimon: Aaah! ...Sorry, you made Paimon jump...
Paimon: Hehe, Paimon was counting her Mora. She's been saving up a lot lately! In a few days time, she'll finally have enough to go buy a surfboard from the People of the Springs!
Paimon: Then, Paimon can zip and zoom along the Spiritways, just like Mualani!
{NICKNAME}: ...Spiritway surfing? You?
Paimon: Well, yeah... You don't sound very happy about it, what's wrong?
{NICKNAME}: I'm gonna miss you, that's all. I've enjoyed traveling with you... So many happy memories.
Paimon: Wait, what!? Stop making it sound like Paimon won't survive!
Paimon: Paimon's thought this through, y'know. Even if she falls off, it'll be fine — 'cause Paimon can fly!
Paimon: Mualani definitely has it harder in that sense... How does she even do it? The Spiritways get so steep and go so high, but she makes it look really easy.
{NICKNAME}: I don't think Mualani finds it hard at all, actually. You can tell by the big smile she has on her face even while performing highly complex maneuvers.
Paimon: Wait, so it's not hard, and Paimon's just... useless? ...That's worse!
voices.title: About Spiritways...

voices.text:
Paimon: So it turns out they use the Pilgrimage to select the Pyro Archon!
Paimon: If Paimon was allowed to compete, maybe even she'd have a shot at becoming the Pyro Archon.
{NICKNAME}: Heh... That's the spirit, Paimon.
Paimon: Hey now, don't you underestimate Paimon! After all the gods we've come face-to-face with, you'd better believe Paimon's picked up a few of their signature moves!
{NICKNAME}: ...Like what?
Paimon: Like... A Buoyant Breeze, Slow-Cooked Bamboo Shoot Soup, Halvamazd, Pour la Justice...
{NICKNAME}: Ohh... you mean their signature dishes.
Paimon: Exactly! They should totally add a cook-off stage to the Pilgrimage! Once everything's settled down in Natlan, of course.
Paimon: Paimon can't wait to get a taste of the Pyro Archon's cooking!
voices.title: About the Pyro Archon...

voices.text:
Paimon: You know who we haven't seen in a while? Xilonen. Last time we saw her, she was lying down in a tree fast asleep.
{NICKNAME}: And the time before that, she was sunbathing on the roof wearing sunglasses.
Paimon: And the time before that, she was chilling in her home-made rocking chair, sipping fruit juice...
Paimon: That's weird, how come our only memories of Xilonen are of her taking a break?
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... It could be that those memories only stand out because they're so unusual. Maybe she's such a hard worker that she doesn't take breaks very often.
Paimon: You think? Huh. Well, speaking of hard workers, Paimon's been finding herself in that category quite a lot recently.
Paimon: Like when we were chasing down that baby Tepetlisaur. Paimon had to fly up pretty darn high to show you the way.
Paimon: And also the time when we went Cacahuatl-picking, and helped that messenger from the Scions of the Canopy look for their package... Whew, if anything, Paimon's been working TOO hard.
Paimon: Hmph, Paimon's gonna be doing a lot more slacking off during our commissions from now on. But secretly, so you won't notice!
{NICKNAME}: You slack off all you need, Paimon. I'll make sure I don't notice.
Paimon: Aww, that's so nice of you! In that case... whenever you're slacking off, Paimon will make sure not to notice you, either!
Paimon: Although actually... It might be easier if we just slacked off together...
Paimon: Alright, new plan! We'll slack off at the same time, but without watching each other. C'mon, let's go, it's sunbathing time!
voices.title: About Taking a Break...

voices.text: Hyah!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XVI

voices.text: Time to ignite!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XVII

voices.text: Scorch and burn!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XVIII

voices.text: Haah!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XIX

voices.text: Honed in flame!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XX

voices.text: Blazing light!
voices.title: Elemental Skill: XXI

voices.text: Ha!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XVI

voices.text: A new dawn rises!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XVII

voices.text: By everlasting flame!
voices.title: Elemental Burst: XVIII

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon heard that the Frostmoon Scions worship the moon. So, what do you think they get up to during the daytime?
{NICKNAME}: Uhh... just go about their normal lives, I guess?
Paimon: No way, not if they're up all night worshiping! Paimon bets they have a really unusual daily routine.
{NICKNAME}: Unusual how?
Paimon: Like, uh... When the sun comes up, they probably shapeshift into huge boulders and take a nice long nap.
Paimon: When night falls, they wake back up again — and with a swish and a swoosh, they're back in human form! Then, they sneak away to start getting up to their secret, mysterious work...
{NICKNAME}: So let me guess — the worst-case scenario for them is blowing through nap time and doing an all-day and all-nighter?
Paimon: Yeah, exactly! See, you got it!
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, I got it... You're getting mixed up between "Scion" and "Sayu" again.
voices.title: About the Frostmoon Scions

voices.text:
Paimon: You know how some people from the Frostmoon Scions have antlers on their heads?
Paimon: In Paimon's view, that's a good sign. 'Cause if you think about it, over the years, everyone else we've met with horns or antlers has turned out to be a total legend!
{NICKNAME}: Yeah, you're right... From the bull warrior of the Collective of Plenty to the Oni King of Hanamizaka, they all share one thing in common...
Paimon: Which is?
{NICKNAME}: You'd better get out of the way, before they... STAMPEEEEDE!
Paimon: Whoooa, yeah! So, do you think that if Lauma ever got really mad, she'd...
Paimon: ...Wait, no, that's ridiculous. Paimon can't picture that happening, like... ever.
{NICKNAME}: Me neither. But at the same time, I can't get the image out of my head...
Paimon: ...Okay, well now Paimon's imagining it too...
Paimon: Ugh, what even is this conversation? Clearly, this is what happens when Paimon goes hungry. We need snacks, pronto!
voices.title: About People With Antlers

voices.text:
Paimon: Aino definitely lives up to her reputation as a whiz-kid mechanic. Everything she builds is so... creative.
Paimon: She uses unlikely materials and slightly wacky designs, but all her inventions work even better than expected!
{NICKNAME}: Which invention have you fallen in love with now, Paimon?
Paimon: The cleaner bot's pretty cool!
Paimon: We should get her to build one for us. It would be really handy to have in the Serenitea Pot!
{NICKNAME}: Really, just the cleaner bot?
Paimon: Hmm, you're right! We might as well make the most of Aino's talents. Let's get a dish-washer bot, a tidy-up bot, a gardener, and one to feed the pets...
Paimon: While we're at it, it'd be great to get a chat bot, too. That way, Tubby will have someone to talk to when we're not around.
{NICKNAME}: Good idea. Anything else to add?
Paimon: Let's see... We could get a cooking bot? Something like the supreme cuisine machine, y'know? It'd be nice to have the option, but of course, there's no substitute for your home cooking, hehe.
Paimon: Although, all these robots everywhere would take up a lot of space... Maybe it'd be better if we got Aino to combine them all into a single machine!
{NICKNAME}: So basically, you want a multifunctional robot for domestic application... Better known as Ineffa.
Paimon: Huh? Wait, you're right... Ineffa can do all of that stuff...
{NICKNAME}: All that, and far more.
{NICKNAME}: She even makes a pretty good travel guide...
Paimon: Uhh... You're not seriously thinking of giving Paimon's job to someone else, are you!?
Paimon: No, no, no, that could never work! There's only one Ineffa, and she has to take care of Aino. We can't separate them!
