Paimon: Don't get Paimon wrong, Ineffa's great, but, but... being a housekeeper in the Serenitea Pot would be too easy for her, don't you think? It'd be a real shame for all that talent to go to waste.
{NICKNAME}: Okay, okay... Paimon is the best guide I could ever hope for, and no one's ever gonna separate us.
Paimon: Hmph. That's more like it.
voices.title: About the Whiz-Kid Mechanic

voices.text:
Paimon: The boss of the Curatorium of Secrets, huh? Now there's a conundrum...
{NICKNAME}: Yeah... Nefer does seem pretty mysterious.
Paimon: That's true, but what Paimon really meant was... Don't you think it's possible that the real boss is actually... Ashru the cat?
{NICKNAME}: Huh? What are you basing that theory on?
Paimon: Well, 'cause it's like how the boss of Komore Teahouse is Taroumaru!
Paimon: And if so... Hehe, maybe Ashru has some treasure hidden behind the counter, too!
{NICKNAME}: Ahh, treasure. So that's what this is about. But what does secret treasure have to do with whether Ashru is the boss or not?
Paimon: Simple! The boss usually earns the most out of all the employees, so the boss's treasure is bound to be the most valuable of them all!
{NICKNAME}: Heh, there's always "value" in Paimon's insights.
{NICKNAME}: But I'm afraid to say that all the available intel points to Nefer being the real boss. So why don't you just go ask her what treasure she has?
Paimon: What? No way, not a chance! ...Ugh, never mind, then.
{NICKNAME}: Hmm? Why the sudden change of heart?
Paimon: Well, obviously 'cause...
Paimon: ...Paimon's too scared.
Paimon: Paimon gets so nervous around her. When Nefer looks you in the eyes, it feels like she's gazing right into your soul... Paimon's gut tells her that she's one of those people you should never, ever get on the wrong side of...
{NICKNAME}: I'm with you there. We should play it safe... Let's go back to plan A, and see if we can figure out where Ashru's treasure is hidden.
Paimon: Aha! So YOU were after Ashru's treasure this whole time, too!
voices.title: About the Boss of the Curatorium of Secrets

voices.text:
Paimon: Paimon heard that Nod-Krai is where the Treasure Hoarders were first founded. Hmph, it's just a fancy name for a bunch of common thieves!
Paimon: If Paimon ever found their headquarters, she'd bust in there and give 'em what for! Y'know, in the name of justice, and all that!
{NICKNAME}: Oh yeah? And what kind of justice would crime-buster Paimon be dishing out?
Paimon: Hehe, poetic justice, of course! Paimon read somewhere that that means giving the bad guys a taste of their own medicine.
Paimon: So Paimon would track down every bit of treasure they're hoarding at their base, and steal it all! See how THEY like having their treasure taken from them!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... Then lemme ask you this — if you stole all their treasure, wouldn't that just make you another treasure hoarder in their eyes?
Paimon: Uh... Maybe? Yeah, kinda...
{NICKNAME}: Oh dear... I'm sorry to say that makes you no better than a common thief, Paimon. And for the sake of justice, I would feel compelled to punish this heinous crime by seizing your secret stash of treasure myself! Hooray for {NICKNAME}, putting the world to rights once again!
Paimon: Hey! That isn't justice, that's plain old justifying!
voices.title: About the Treasure Hoarders

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: Did you know that the first group to conquer Nasha Town was the Conch Gang? Or so the story goes.
Paimon: The Conch Gang? You mean, that gang where they're all kids?
{NICKNAME}: That's right. In fact, they only accept children as members, and after you get to a certain age, they kick you out. That's their gang tradition — it's been that way from the very beginning.
Paimon: Wait, so you're saying that a bunch of kids took over Nasha Town!? What a funny thought... They must've been some pretty tough kids! Did they have superpowers or something?
{NICKNAME}: Umm... I don't think so. At least, the story I heard didn't mention anything about that.
Paimon: Then how the heck did a bunch of kids conquer a whole town in Nod-Krai?
{NICKNAME}: I guess they just hung out and played games in what's now the market square. There probably weren't any shops in Nasha Town back then.
Paimon: That doesn't sound much like "conquering"...
{NICKNAME}: Before long, the grown-ups took a liking to the place... Slowly but surely, the children's Elysium was engulfed by the adult world...
Paimon: Couldn't they just... find somewhere else to play?
{NICKNAME}: That's easier said than done... I mean, imagine if one day, you suddenly found that your favorite nap spot in the whole garden had been taken over by hilichurls.
{NICKNAME}: Once a cozy patch of lawn, now a camp full of rowdy hilichurls who throw pebbles at you to keep you away... You'd never be able to nap in your favorite spot, ever again...
Paimon: Nooo! That's terrible! Paimon was there first! Stupid hilichurls... Oh, and stupid grown-ups!
Paimon: So... what happened after that? Did the Conch Gang fight back?
{NICKNAME}: I'm not too sure. It's possible that they tried, but... I suspect that when the kids in the gang grew up, they had to make a living somehow, so they ended up turning into the same adults that they once saw as their enemies.
Paimon: Oh... Well that took a depressing turn...
{NICKNAME}: To be honest, it's probably not a true story. The Conch Gang of today, on the other hand — they seem to be doing great. They have a lot of members and some pretty good benefits.
Paimon: Ooh, benefits? Hehe, can Paimon join?
{NICKNAME}: Oh, I'm sure you'd have no problem getting in! And if you don't like it, I heard that you can leave at any time.
Paimon: Not a "homies for life" type of gang, then...
{NICKNAME}: You know, I think it would suit you.
{NICKNAME}: Adults are so set in their ways, whereas children are lovable little people who are free to be themselves... just like you, Paimon.
voices.title: Tell me about the Conch Gang...

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: I've got the latest issue of the Nasha Express here. Let's see what's in it...
Paimon: Ooh, Nod-Krai has a newspaper too? Well, what does it say? Is it full of juicy stories like The Steambird?
Paimon: Hehe, Nod-Krai's pretty chaotic compared to Fontaine. The news here must be crazy!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm...
Paimon: Don't worry, even if it's heavy going, Paimon can handle it! Paimon wouldn't be surprised if it's nothing but crime from cover to cover.
{NICKNAME}: Oh...
Paimon: ...Of course, if there's any super creepy, nightmare-fuel-type stories... maybe don't tell Paimon those.
Paimon: ...What is it? Why aren't you saying anything? It's not... it's not ALL super creepy nightmare fuel, is it!?
{NICKNAME}: No, there's no nightmare fuel. It's not so much "creepy"... it's just plain weird.
{NICKNAME}: For example: "The Flagship is seeking a new bartender. Must have cocktail-mixing experience. Salary negotiable. Preference for candidates who are patient, hard of hearing, and good at taking notes."
{NICKNAME}: "Mimisbrunnr Books is holding a clearance sale. Many old titles for sale by the kilogram at bargain prices. Browse first at no charge. Please note: Established authors, budding authors, or any other type of authors should not use this as an opportunity to advertise your work, or you may find your stock being sold off dirt cheap by the kilogram too."
{NICKNAME}: "New flower seeds now available at Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse. Each purchase comes with a full suite of essentials to keep your plant in tip-top condition: 1 can of engine oil, 1 bag of rust, and 1 pair of cut-resistant gloves. Limited stock available on a first-come, first-served basis."
Paimon: What kind of flower needs oil and rust!?
Paimon: Aren't newspapers supposed to report the news? This just seems like a classifieds section gone mad.
{NICKNAME}: Pretty fun though, right? A little window into daily life in Nod-Krai.
Paimon: All that says to Paimon is that the people here live very strange and very confusing lives...
{NICKNAME}: Well... What is life if not the thread between events that offers some semblance of order amidst chaos? The through-line that we cling to in an effort to traverse the maze that is the cosmos?
Paimon: Honestly, whatever you just said went completely over Paimon's head. Let's stick with the newspaper for now. Any other interesting ads?
{NICKNAME}: Umm... Ah, here we go! There's some good news and some bad news — which do you want to hear first?
Paimon: Uhh... The good news?
{NICKNAME}: "Seeking game-testers for a paid position. Flat rate per session. Perks include free lunch, free dinner, and a small gift at the end of each session."
Paimon: That sounds pretty cool! Hehe, we should definitely check that out! Let's apply quick before someone else gets it!
{NICKNAME}: First things first, Paimon — the bad news. Which also happens to be related to the game-tester position.
Paimon: What is it? *sigh* Did they fill all the positions already?
{NICKNAME}: The ad was posted by a researcher from the Fontaine Research Institute by the name of... Liouba.
Paimon: Okay, time to throw that paper away, {NICKNAME}. Let's head to Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse and check out this flower that you're apparently supposed to oil instead of water.
voices.title: About the Nasha Express

voices.text:
Paimon: Nod-Krai seems like a pretty complicated place. There are tons of people from all over Teyvat here.
Paimon: We've seen people from Liyue, Fontaine, Sumeru, Inazuma... Even Natlan!
Paimon: Wait... Hey, how come we've hardly seen any merchants from Mondstadt here? That doesn't seem right.
Paimon: Mondstadt's the wine capital of the world, right? You'd think someone would be making a killing off of that out here.
{NICKNAME}: Maybe Mondstadt wine isn't really designed for exporting. Most of it's brewed and enjoyed locally. It might lose its flavor when transported long distances.
{NICKNAME}: And even if someone managed to solve that problem, the cost of shipping it all this way would mean they'd have to increase the price, which would make it harder to sell... Maybe it's simply too difficult to turn a profit.
Paimon: You think? Hehe... Paimon's theory was that Mondstadters drink so much, there's none left to export.
{NICKNAME}: Um... That could be part of the reason, for sure. They can't get enough of their wine, can they?
Paimon: Hey, the next time we go back to Mondstadt, we should bring some Nod-Krai liquor with us.
Paimon: Yeah... the strongest one, and then get Charles to trick Kaeya into drinking it by masking the flavor with some other drink.
Paimon: While we're at it, we should get gifts for other people too. A ragdoll for Klee, and how about a little robot for Sucrose? Might come in handy with her research!
Paimon: Oh yeah — and remember those red goggles we saw that time? Maybe a pair of those for Amber?
Paimon: You know what — let's go souvenir shopping right now! There's a bunch of other cool gifts Paimon's thinking of getting too... She won't spend all our Mora, promise!
voices.title: About Memories of Mondstadt

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: Let me tell you a story about one of the craziest con games in Nod-Krai's history.
{NICKNAME}: There once was a thief and a conman who heard that a traveling merchant had just arrived in town. This merchant was said to be extremely wealthy and a big spender — meaning he'd brought a huge stash of valuables and Mora with him. And so, the thief and the conman decided to team up to try and steal the merchant's wealth.
Paimon: Uh-oh. How far did they get?
{NICKNAME}: After working to gain the merchant's trust, the conman invited the merchant out to a big dinner party one evening. The plan was to get him away from his shop for long enough for the thief to break in and steal all the treasure... And it went off without a hitch.
Paimon: ...Aw, poor merchant.
{NICKNAME}: But the story doesn't end there. The con artist wanted all the loot for himself. He turned on the thief, threatened him into handing everything over, and then sold him out. The thief took the fall and wound up in jail.
Paimon: Huh. Behind every crook is an even crooked-er crook. So in the end, the conman conned both the merchant and the thief... and by the sounds of it, he got away with it too? Ugh...
{NICKNAME}: Now, your typical crime story would probably end there. But not this one...
Paimon: There's more?
{NICKNAME}: After the conman finally got his hands on the treasure, he discovered that it was all fake! He started to panic... and then, the merchant comes bursting through the door, demanding that his assets be returned.
Paimon: Wait, but they were fake, right? Why did he want them back?
{NICKNAME}: Obviously, the merchant claimed that everything stolen by the thief was real. So in the end, the conman was forced to return genuine treasure, and not the fake stuff.
Paimon: Ohh... So the merchant was the real conman in that story! Heh, so much for "poor merchant."
{NICKNAME}: True, but if the conman and the thief hadn't given in to their crooked ways, the merchant would never have done anything to them. So the moral of this story is:
Paimon: If you're gonna play the con game, you gotta go big or go home!
{NICKNAME}: ...Actually, it's "don't give in to your crooked ways"...
voices.title: About the Art of the Con

voices.text:
Paimon: So, you know how Ineffa's a robot?
Paimon: Paimon's been wondering... Do you think she has an on-off switch?
{NICKNAME}: I've never seen it, but... probably, I guess?
Paimon: Wow... Paimon's sooo jealous.
{NICKNAME}: Why?
Paimon: Well, think about it. Ineffa goes to wake Aino up in the morning, but Aino wants to sleep in. All Aino has to do is...
{NICKNAME}: ...Flip Ineffa's off switch so she powers down?
Paimon: Exactly!
Paimon: {NICKNAME}, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's bestest buddy in the whole wide world! Can you get Aino to make you an on-off switch too?
{NICKNAME}: Sure!
Paimon: Huh? You're just gonna say yes without even asking why?
{NICKNAME}: I think I already know why. You want to flip my off switch when you feel like sleeping in!
Paimon: What!? You saw right through Paimon's plan...
{NICKNAME}: The thing is, after all the spare parts I've thrown her way, I've pretty much got Aino in my pocket...
{NICKNAME}: So although it would look like an off switch, it would actually activate my emergency mode. And then I'd... suddenly spring into action and start tickling you mercilessly! Protest all you want, Paimon — the tickling cannot be stopped!
Paimon: No, noooo! We're not getting you an on-off switch, okay? Happy now?
voices.title: About Ineffa's On-Off Switch

voices.text:
Paimon: Aino's inventions are a real bargain!
{NICKNAME}: That's because she builds them from scrap, which has no value to anyone else.
Paimon: Paimon was thinking, maybe we should get Aino to build us a hoverboard... 'cause then, you'd be able to fly just like Paimon!
Paimon: It would make the rest of your journey way easier. We could just fly the whole way!
{NICKNAME}: Wow, what an amazing idea, Paimon! So, what's your budget?
Paimon: Uh... Paimon only has 500 Mora left after last week... B—But Aino might still be able to find a way, right?
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... That's a pretty tight budget. At this rate, our hoverboard might have to be powered by a potato battery...
Paimon: Mmm... Potato-powered aviation... *drools*
Paimon: ...Wait, hold up, a potato battery? Is that a real thing?
voices.title: About Aino's Inventions

voices.text:
Paimon: Flins gives the best compliments!
Paimon: Paimon could listen to his flattery all day... Ah, that would be the best day ever!
{NICKNAME}: Very true. You're so attentive, Paimon, and you always see the best in people. That's why you have a knack for identifying people's finer qualities.
Paimon: Hee-hee, too right! Attentive Paimon always sees the best in people!
{NICKNAME}: Not to mention the courage and dedication you've shown in keeping me company all this time. You always see things through, even when it's hard work, and you've never abandoned me even when mortal danger is staring us in the face.
Paimon: Aw, shucks, you really mean that?
{NICKNAME}: On top of all that, you're as smart as you are sweet. The idea of traveling without Paimon by my side is too terrible to even contemplate.
Paimon: C'mon, {NICKNAME}, knock it off, y—you're making Paimon blush...
{NICKNAME}: Okay, three compliments in and you're as red as a tomato. Imagine what a full day of compliments from Flins would do to you...
Paimon: Waaah! Whew, thanks, but no thanks!
voices.title: About Flattery

voices.text:
Paimon: Those Sniffer Moles have a really keen sense of smell, huh? They're experts when it comes to foraging for berries.
Paimon: We should get some as pets! Hehe, then we could have all the Lakkaberries and Midsommar Berries we wanted!
Paimon: And then you could make Krumkakes and Midsommar Torte for Paimon every day!
{NICKNAME}: It's a nice idea, but Sniffer Moles are wild animals. Would they really make good pets?
Paimon: Hehe, don't you worry about that, Paimon's got it all figured out!
Paimon: Back in Sumeru, Paimon read this book from the Amurta Darshan which said that if you raise an animal from a young enough age, they'll treat you like family.
Paimon: So let's go find some young whipper-snapper Sniffer Moles and raise 'em right!
{NICKNAME}: Hmm... In that case, it'd probably be a few months before they were old enough to fend for themselves.
{NICKNAME}: Obviously, we'd need to feed them properly during that time... and as we know, their diet is mostly Lakkaberries and Midsommar Berries.
{NICKNAME}: So by the time they're all grown up, Paimon's stash of Lakkaberry Krumkakes and Midsommar Torte will be completely decimated.
Paimon: Waaah! Noooo! Ugh, why did you have to turn this into a horror story?
voices.title: About Sniffer Moles

voices.text:
Paimon: So, we finally met Varka. Long time coming, huh? When was the first time we heard his name?
Paimon: Let's see... It definitely wasn't the letter that Ineffa gave us, or when we heard him on the Dodocommunication Device. Was it when Mika read out that letter to the Knights of Favonius? ...No, Paimon's pretty sure Jean mentioned him long before that...
{NICKNAME}: I actually read a book about him in the Mondstadt library once. It was called, "100 Things You Never Knew About Varka."
Paimon: Really? What was it about? A list of all his heroic accomplishments, or something?
{NICKNAME}: That's right, yeah. It was a while ago now, lemme see what I can remember... Ah, yes. There was one bit that said:
{NICKNAME}: "Varka can chug three hundred Dandelion Wines in a row without getting drunk!"
{NICKNAME}: "...Mainly because he drinks them so quickly that the alcohol doesn't have time to kick in."
Paimon: What the hecking heck? Really stretching the definition of heroic there... What else did it say?
{NICKNAME}: "Varka is the only man in the whole of Mondstadt who's ever defeated the city walls in a game of Ludi Harpastum."
Paimon: Huh...
{NICKNAME}: "Varka once won a fight against ten Ruin Guards. Six of them were destroyed by his fishing rod, three of them by the stool he was sitting on..."
{NICKNAME}: "...And the last one thought it had been destroyed, even though it hadn't — but it still counts."
Paimon: Huh... You know, what's weird is that all of this stuff obviously sounds like a bunch of baloney...
Paimon: ...And yet, having actually met Varka in person, it all... kinda makes sense...
Paimon: Wait a second... Do we think that maybe... he wrote this book himself?
Paimon: Next time we're in Mondstadt, our first priority is to head to the library, find Lisa, and borrow that book. Then, we'll take it to Varka and demand answers!
{NICKNAME}: In that case, we'll have to rename it as: 101 Things You Never Knew About Varka.
Paimon: Really? Why? What's the hundred-and-first thing?
{NICKNAME}: "'100 Things You Never Knew About Varka' isn't even a real book. That's the one thing that even Varka never knew about Varka — but of course, the book would never dare break the news to him."
voices.title: About 100 Things You Never Knew About Varka

voices.text:
Paimon: "The Northern Intelligence Network"... What a mysterious-sounding organization!
Paimon: A secret society, quietly pulling the strings behind the scenes, running the entire world from the shadows!
{NICKNAME}: "Secret society" seems like a stretch. We know a whole bunch of the people involved.
Paimon: ...Ohh yeah, we do! Hey, this could be our foot in the door! We should totally join, then we can get one of those cool codenames! Like... ummm... Ooh, White Gold!
{NICKNAME}: Oh, because you have white hair and I have blond hair... An unusually sensible nickname, for once.
Paimon: Well, yeah! This is our own nickname! The weird ones are reserved for other people.
Paimon: Actually, don't the Knights of Favonius work with the intelligence network? What do you think Varka's codename is? "Grand Master"?
Paimon: Heh, it's kind of hard to imagine Grand Master Varka doing spy stuff, isn't it? He's not exactly a low-key kinda guy...
Paimon: He'd probably go busting into the enemy base through the front gates, mowing down all the minions in his path, and then strut his way out with a briefcase full of intel in hand.
{NICKNAME}: ...I suspect that, as Grand Master, he probably delegates that kind of work to people like Kaeya and Rosaria.
Paimon: Oh, good point! ...Wait, you're right, this isn't a secret society at all! More like a... who's-who of... people we know already!
voices.title: About the Northern Intelligence Network: Codenames

voices.text:
Paimon: The cool codenames they use in the Northern Intelligence Network kinda remind Paimon of the ancient names back in Natlan.
{NICKNAME}: Uhh... I mean, sure, they're both pseudonyms, but beyond that... do they really have any similarities?
Paimon: Sure they do! They're both, y'know... cool!
Paimon: Although, the Natlanese version is definitely cooler, 'cause they get a phlogiston engraving on their body too.
Paimon: And when it's time for action, they go "poof" and light up like a lantern! It's like, yep, that person's definitely the hero in this situation, hehe!
Paimon: Just like Varesa when she puts on her mask!
{NICKNAME}: Speaking of masked heroes... that reminds me of someone else involved with the intelligence network.
Paimon: Lemme guess — Master Diluc?
{NICKNAME}: Yep. Hey, how about we bring him with us to Natlan next time we visit? We should get someone to make a phlogiston engraving for him.
Paimon: Hehehe, that's an awesome idea! It probably won't light up, since he's from Mondstadt... but hey — it'd still be pretty cool!
{NICKNAME}: The next time he's out fighting crime, he won't have to lift a finger. Just a glimpse of that phlogiston engraving will have those cowardly crooks curled up in a fetal position on the ground.
Paimon: Oh yeah... Oh, actually no. The Darknight Hero can't go around being too flashy, or he might blow his cover...
{NICKNAME}: True... Yeah, on second thought, there's a lot of issues with this plan.
{NICKNAME}: The biggest one being: How do we get Diluc to Natlan and back in one piece? He'd melt in the heat, unless we can convince him to change out of that fancy suit.
voices.title: About the Northern Intelligence Network: Heroes

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: Come to think of it, we've met not one but two genius inventors in Nod-Krai, haven't we? First Aino, and then Sandrone.
Paimon: Yeah, you're right. And the proof of their genius is in the hi-tech pudding: Ineffa Pudding and Pulonia Pudding!
Paimon: Actually... Okay, well "Pulonia Pudding" kinda works, Paimon's not gonna lose any sleep over that one... but Ineffa Pudding feels a little disrespectful...
{NICKNAME}: I'm speechless... After years of giving people ugly nicknames, you're finally learning! Yes, Paimon, name-calling IS disrespectful!
Paimon: Hey!
{NICKNAME}: Seriously though, who do you think would win in a fight between Ineffa the Annihilator and Pulonia the Pulverizer?
Paimon: Are you for real!? Who's the name-caller now, huh!? Also, fantasizing about violence is a way worse habit than giving people ugly nicknames...
Paimon: ...Honestly, though? After everything that's happened recently, it's hard to imagine them getting into a fight. Everyone's getting along pretty well these days.
Paimon: It's just as dumb as trying to imagine Jean and Diluc in a fight...
{NICKNAME}: I can't believe you still remember that...
{NICKNAME}: Ahem, but anyway... we're getting sidetracked. Back to Ineffa and Pulonia: I've thought of a foolproof way of figuring out who's stronger...
{NICKNAME}: All you'd have to do is lock them both in a room, then drop Lynette inside...
Paimon: What the...!
{NICKNAME}: ...And whoever gets destroyed last is clearly the strongest!
Paimon: Mmm, Paimon's not convinced. Like, sometimes, the more advanced technology is also the more fragile, right?
Paimon: ...Ugh, what are we talking about? Enough! No more imaginary fights between friends!
voices.title: About Strange Technology

voices.text:
{NICKNAME}: I heard Aunt Alice tell a very scary and painful story.
{NICKNAME}: Fair warning, Paimon. You should steel yourself before deciding whether or not you want to listen. Personally, I'd advise against it.
Paimon: What could possibly be that scary!? Paimon doesn't wanna hear it!
Paimon: ...Urgh, but on the other hand, Paimon's curiosity is killing her... Y—Y'know what? Let's hear it!
{NICKNAME}: See? Everyone's like that. The more you warn someone, the more curious they get.
{NICKNAME}: The more you tell them not to think of something, the more they obsess over it.
{NICKNAME}: This is precisely the principle Alice wanted to use to play a prank on Nicole.
Paimon: Huh? Why would she do that?
{NICKNAME}: It seems like Nicole was quite the chatterbox back in the day. Why, she could almost talk your head off.
{NICKNAME}: Aunt Alice wanted to hear what a scream from her might sound like, and how far an unconscious "voice" like hers might reach...
Paimon: Sorry, what kinda weird motive is that!?
{NICKNAME}: And so, she said to Nicole...
Paimon: Yeah?
{NICKNAME}: Seriously, Paimon. Last chance to save yourself...
Paimon: Keep going! Paimon can take it.
{NICKNAME}: She said, "Whatever you do, do not think about having a toothpick wedged between your toenail and toe when you stub it!"
Paimon: Aaaaaah!
{NICKNAME}: Nicole was stunned for a moment, and then she reacted much the same way you did.
{NICKNAME}: Every living being within a 100-meter radius, Alice included, suffered from anauralia for the next few days.
voices.title: About Anauralia
